definitions.explanation: The act of officially taking away someone's property or possessions, usually as a penalty or by authority. Also used in everyday contexts like a teacher confiscating a phone.

examples.japanese: スマホを{没収|ぼっしゅう}された。
{税関|ぜいかん}で{荷物|にもつ}を{没収|ぼっしゅう}された。
examples.english: My luggage was seized at customs.

examples.japanese: {違法|いほう}に{持|も}ち{込|こ}まれた{品物|しなもの}はすべて{没収|ぼっしゅう}の{対象|たいしょう}となる。
examples.english: All illegally imported goods are subject to confiscation.

notes: In sports, {没収|ぼっしゅう}{試合|しあい} means a forfeited game. In legal contexts, {没収|ぼっしゅう} refers to the seizure of property as part of a criminal penalty. In everyday life, it commonly describes a teacher confiscating a student's belongings. Common collocations: {財産|ざいさん}を{没収|ぼっしゅう}する (to confiscate assets), {没収|ぼっしゅう}{試合|しあい} (forfeited game), {没収|ぼっしゅう}{処分|しょぶん} (confiscation penalty).
